body:
The Republic we learned about in school has been taken hostage by a tyrannical minority of politicians and lobbyists.

| Peter,

This is going to be a longer email, but it’s really important. I hope you’ll take a couple minutes to read. I want to talk about the huge challenges facing our democracy.

[_**But if you don’t have the time to read and you still want to make a donation to help Leaders We Deserve elect more young people who are committed to addressing those challenges, you can click here to split a donation between Leaders We Deserve and Fight for Progress.**_](https://click.everyaction.com/k/75633550/445279678/139938695?refcode=BLU_EM_FFP_2023-12-22_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNS8xLzc3NDA2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjllYWRmZmMyLWRhYTAtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyM2YzNiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZkJcG1uzH8gtv3JOfd9q7uf9VtJgV5sTSPSD-5ZUj20=)

Today, the Republic we learned about in school has been taken hostage by a tyrannical minority of politicians and lobbyists who have pledged allegiance to the powerful, not the people. They act to placate special interests that are destroying our planet, endangering our schools, and seeking to tighten their stranglehold on our suffocating democracy — all in the name of profit.

Young Americans have grown up witnessing this. Previous generations saw the horrors of war, racial injustice, and the assassination of our greatest leaders broadcast into their homes on TV. In contrast, we hold in our hands—on our phones—the horror of school shootings, attempted insurrections, hate crimes like those in Buffalo, El Paso, and too many others, as well as the wrath of climate change.

Yet, like our forebears, we refuse to accept that the America we were born into is the best we can achieve. We’ve protested by the millions, leading walkouts and marches to demand action on gun violence in every community, and we’ve staged sit-ins for climate action, demanding police accountability for the extrajudicial killings of our fellow Americans.

Young Americans have also voted at the highest rates in our history over the past three elections. We do so because we believe, contrary to what Fox News tells our grandparents, that America's best days lie ahead, not behind us. We know that our democracy is broken, but it’s not unfixable. **We also know that no one else will come to save us — we must save ourselves and become the leaders we don’t have.**

I believe the greatest threat to our democracy is not a single individual, such as Donald Trump. **The real danger is the hopelessness** that elevates such figures and the failure of our government to deliver for its people, fueling that despair. It's concerning to see an increasing number of Americans, both young and old, yearning for "one good politician who's not corrupt to come and fix it all," not realizing that such a day could herald the rise of a dictator.

Gen Z has been educated about democracy in our civics classes while simultaneously preparing for active shooter drills, reflecting a democracy that has failed to ensure our safety. **If we don't address this and empower more young people who understand the anxiety of these drills and who can inject much-needed hope into our democracy, we risk losing it altogether.** If our democracy fails to fulfill our most basic expectations — keeping us safe — voters may turn to someone who promises security while endangering democracy itself.

**That’s why I co-founded Leaders We Deserve.** We are striving to elect young leaders who believe our country's best days are ahead, who envision a government that truly serves its people, understanding that poor governance is a result of poor leadership. For too long, many politicians have been propped up by special interests who claim government doesn't work, only to be elected and ensure its failure.

That’s one of the biggest reasons we refuse to accept corporate money, relying instead on the vast majority of our funds from small donors. We help recruit, staff, substantially fund, and provide volunteers for the campaigns of young Democrats under 30 running for state legislatures and Congress.

If we can change the face of our government and elect more young leaders who understand the gravity of the problems we’re facing, we may finally be able to make the progress we need to overcome them. But the work we’re doing takes a lot of resources, Peter, and we’re counting on your support to keep going.

[_**So if you’re with us in the fight to ensure our democracy survives for future generations, and if you’re able, please split a donation between Leaders We Deserve and Fight for Progress.**_](https://click.everyaction.com/k/75633551/445279679/139938695?refcode=BLU_EM_FFP_2023-12-22_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNS8xLzc3NDA2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjllYWRmZmMyLWRhYTAtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyM2YzNiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZkJcG1uzH8gtv3JOfd9q7uf9VtJgV5sTSPSD-5ZUj20=)

clean_body: The Republic we learned about in school has been taken hostage by a tyrannical minority of politicians and lobbyists. | Peter, This is going to be a longer email, but it’s really important. I hope you’ll take a couple minutes to read. I want to talk about the huge challenges facing our democracy. = Today, the Republic we learned about in school has been taken hostage by a tyrannical minority of politicians and lobbyists who have pledged allegiance to the powerful, not the people. They act to placate special interests that are destroying our planet, endangering our schools, and seeking to tighten their stranglehold on our suffocating democracy — all in the name of profit. Young Americans have grown up witnessing this. Previous generations saw the horrors of war, racial injustice, and the assassination of our greatest leaders broadcast into their homes on TV. In contrast, we hold in our hands—on our phones—the horror of school shootings, attempted insurrections, hate crimes like those in Buffalo, El Paso, and too many others, as well as the wrath of climate change. Yet, like our forebears, we refuse to accept that the America we were born into is the best we can achieve. We’ve protested by the millions, leading walkouts and marches to demand action on gun violence in every community, and we’ve staged sit-ins for climate action, demanding police accountability for the extrajudicial killings of our fellow Americans. Young Americans have also voted at the highest rates in our history over the past three elections. We do so because we believe, contrary to what Fox News tells our grandparents, that America's best days lie ahead, not behind us. We know that our democracy is broken, but it’s not unfixable. We also know that no one else will come to save us — we must save ourselves and become the leaders we don’t have. I believe the greatest threat to our democracy is not a single individual, such as Donald Trump. The real danger is the hopelessness that elevates such figures and the failure of our government to deliver for its people, fueling that despair. It's concerning to see an increasing number of Americans, both young and old, yearning for "one good politician who's not corrupt to come and fix it all," not realizing that such a day could herald the rise of a dictator. Gen Z has been educated about democracy in our civics classes while simultaneously preparing for active shooter drills, reflecting a democracy that has failed to ensure our safety. If we don't address this and empower more young people who understand the anxiety of these drills and who can inject much-needed hope into our democracy, we risk losing it altogether. If our democracy fails to fulfill our most basic expectations — keeping us safe — voters may turn to someone who promises security while endangering democracy itself. That’s why I co-founded Leaders We Deserve. We are striving to elect young leaders who believe our country's best days are ahead, who envision a government that truly serves its people, understanding that poor governance is a result of poor leadership. For too long, many politicians have been propped up by special interests who claim government doesn't work, only to be elected and ensure its failure. That’s one of the biggest reasons we refuse to accept corporate money, relying instead on the vast majority of our funds from small donors. We help recruit, staff, substantially fund, and provide volunteers for the campaigns of young Democrats under 30 running for state legislatures and Congress. If we can change the face of our government and elect more young leaders who understand the gravity of the problems we’re facing, we may finally be able to make the progress we need to overcome them. But the work we’re doing takes a lot of resources, Peter, and we’re counting on your support to keep going. = | = | = | = | = | = Thank you for your support, Firstname. body:
Hey there,
I wanted to make sure you saw my team’s email about how we’re tackling our online fundraising goals this month. Over the next few days, people will start going officially offline for the holidays (including myself!) to spend time with family and relax before the New Year.
That means we can’t count on the normal flood of last-minute support in the last few days before our FEC fundraising deadline on December 31st. So we’re adjusting our strategy accordingly, increasing our outreach earlier in the month than we normally do. With every campaign and store in the country sending out emails, we are doing our best to hit our goals.
[**I’m writing because I would really love to earn your support as we wrap up 2023 and head into the 2024 election year. Your support would be a help to ensuring we reach our goals and continue building the strongest campaign possible.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-dec23.ZG_uWI&refcode=em231222-1-tt&t=1&akid=939%2E135344%2ErZTrXc)**

Thank you,
Elissa Slotkin

To: dpwillis67@gmail.com _
Team, It’s hard to believe, but we are fully in December: Towns across Michigan are decorated with twinkling lights, local businesses are filled with gifts, and it feels like holiday parties are back to pre-COVID levels.
Add it all up, and it’s fully the holiday season. But that also means something else: We are quickly approaching our final FEC deadline before the 2024 election year officially kicks off.
We know what the hustle and bustle of the holidays means: These emails will get opened less and less as the month goes on. Here on Team Slotkin, we’re realists, so we wanted to walk you through our shift in plans.
As we’ve outlined before, every year candidates running for federal office face four official quarterly fundraising deadlines – March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31. After these deadlines pass, we are legally required to report how much money we’ve raised and the number of donations we receive. We will have to file our fourth quarter report on January 31, 2024.
Once we file our report, our fundraising numbers will be made public and political insiders, reporters, and our opponents will use it as a metric to gauge our strength as we enter the election year.
Typically, we break down a large quarterly goal by month, then break those goals down by weeks. Usually, we plan on raising 25% of our money in October, 25% in November, and 50% in December. But here’s the catch: We raise about 70% of our monthly goal in the last two weeks of the month – as urgency ramps up around the deadline.
With the holidays in December, we have to be much more strategic in how we’re raising – the earlier in the month, the better, because it helps us offset the steep decline in fundraising as people go offline for the holidays.
[**So, how do you fit into this? Well, the majority of our individual contributions come through emails like this one. And if everyone reading this gave $3 now, we’d certainly be on track to hit our December goal before our FEC deadline this month.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-dec23.ZG_uWI&refcode=em231222-1-tt&t=3&akid=939%2E135344%2ErZTrXc)**

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

A new Axios article hammers home how centrist Democrats and anti-Palestine
groups like AIPAC are plotting revenge against our progressive movement in
2024, in light of our Justice Democrats candidates taking a strong
anti-war stance and demanding a permanent ceasefire in Israel and
Palestine.

The first step in their three-pronged strategy to maintain the status quo
is to “spend heavily to defeat "Squad"-like Democrats.”

Incumbents like Summer Lee, Cori Bush, Jamaal Bowman, and Ilhan Omar
already have candidates lined up to challenge them in next year’s
Democratic primaries; of course, those moderate challengers are backed by
groups like AIPAC and Democratic Majority for Israel PAC, who are funded
by right-wing millionaires and Trump donors.

Meanwhile, AIPAC is reportedly still recruiting candidates to take on
other Squad members like Rashida Tlaib to punish them for their pro-peace
stance.

Like Axios reports, the Israel-Palestine conflict will clearly take
“center stage” in Democratic primaries next year, and with GOP mega-donor
funded groups like AIPAC preparing to spend more money than ever before to
try and take down the Squad, our progressive movement faces a very real
threat.

If we’re going to re-elect the Squad and continue to build our young,
diverse, working-class bloc of progressives in Congress in 2024, we need
to rapidly build the resources needed to take on the heavily-funded
pro-war, right-wing groups NOW.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20231222.M3y6u8&refcode=em20231222-32453&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1001&akid=32453%2E1203867%2EnlpWGH ]With the end of 2023 approaching in less than two weeks, will you chip

Democrats reach our grassroots fundraising goal of $75,000 before December
31 at midnight?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20231222.M3y6u8&refcode=em20231222-32453&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1020&akid=32453%2E1203867%2EnlpWGH ]Contribute $3

In solidarity,

Geoff Simpson
Campaigns Director

Do not worry if you cannot afford to make a contribution — we understand that
this is a difficult time.

There are other ways to make an impact in support of peace and equality in

using [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/139874?t=1022&akid=32453%2E1203867%2EnlpWGH ]Jewish Voice for Peace’s dialer here. Your voice matters in this

# [](https://go.bobcasey.com/go/181?t=1&akid=1469%2E552475%2E7zlFIr)
Hi Peter,

**From all of us here on Team Casey, happy holidays!**
This holiday season, we hope that you are able to spend time with loved ones enjoying the traditions of your family.
Whether your kids are looking for the glass pickle ornament in your Christmas tree, you’re going to the movies, volunteering at a soup kitchen, having a meal with family, or whatever else your traditions may be, we’re wishing you a joyful holiday season.
As we turn to the New Year, we’re also facing a holiday tradition for campaigns -- an end-of-quarter fundraising deadline. name: Chuck Schumer
subject: The most important race in 2024
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Serve America PAC
body:
Friend, the most important race happening in 2024 isn't just the race for the White House. It's the race for Senate control.
The future of everything we care about – from health care and voting rights to abortion rights – will depend on who holds the Senate majority after the election. That's why I'm writing to you today.
With the retirement of Sen. Joe Manchin, we could hold every single seat we have and still lose Senate control. That's why it's so imperative that we help Colin Allred defeat Ted Cruz in Texas.
Polls are showing these two neck and neck, and Ted Cruz is the most vulnerable GOP senator in the country. We can win this race, but the GOP knows it too – they're preparing to pour millions of dollars into Texas to lie about Colin's record and try to stop us.
Friend, if we can match the GOP's millions, we can win in Texas and virtually guarantee our Senate majority. But if Colin misses his fundraising goals, we'll lose the best chance we have to secure Senate control. Please, I'm personally asking: Will you split a donation of $25 or more between Colin Allred and Serve America to help Colin defeat Ted Cruz and protect our Democratic Senate majority?! [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/serve-allred]
Thank you.
Chuck

name: Katie Porter
subject: I’m calling for a lasting bilateral ceasefire, here’s why
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Katie Porter for Senate
body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/14558?t=1&akid=35163%2E3422442%2E2fto32)
Derek, **I’m calling for a lasting bilateral ceasefire in Gaza.**
It’s painful to witness the human tragedies of the war between Israel and Hamas. While this is a war between Israel and Hamas,**the United States should identify and push for conditions that will make a lasting bilateral ceasefire possible.** These conditions include:
1. A release of all hostages
2. Durable security for Israel
3. An end of Hamas’ control of Gaza

Lasting peace will require a commitment to both economic and humanitarian aid to rebuild Gaza after the war. And, it will require negotiations toward a democratic Palestinian state with full and equal rights for its citizens.
I have long said that durable peace will require a two-state solution and a democratic Palestinian government free from Hamas. Prime Minister Nethanyahu’s recent comments rejecting Palestinian governance of Gaza are especially concerning, as they undermine our country’s longstanding position that a two-state solution is necessary to achieve enduring peace for both Israelis and Palestinians.
**The situation is dire and requires an end to hostilities that threaten to worsen this conflict’s already appalling loss of Palestinian and Israeli lives.** Hamas has allowed Palestinians in Gaza to suffer shortages of food, clean water, fuel, and medicine for years. The current war caused by Hamas’ terrorism has made an already terrible situation for Palestinian civilians so much worse. The rising death toll of Palestinian civilians from infectious diseases and the lack of food, water, and medicine highlight the escalation of this tragedy.
Now, the Biden Administration must encourage a lasting bilateral ceasefire that brings remaining hostages home, secures Israel’s safety, removes Hamas from operational control of Gaza, and invests in creating a better economic and political architecture for Palestinians in Gaza.
In this painful time, we must acknowledge heart-wrenching losses but not give up hope for a better future.
Katie Porter

Friend,
It's the holidays, and we hope you have a restful time planned with family and friends.
But right now, my team and I are reaching out with a request for some urgent support--the holidays are always a particularly scary time for true grassroots candidates, as our fundraising and support takes a big drop as people (rightly!) unplug and take time off to travel.
We launched this campaign only back in October, and we've run a scrappy and strategic operation since: in that short amount of time, we've gotten nearly 2,000 individual donors to endorse my run for Congress in Ohio.
It has been an incredible result, and one that I did not expect, but my staff is a little worried right now and I don't want to let any of you down. Next week is the last week of the quarter, and the end of 2023. We will need to report our numbers, and I don't want to end the year on a low note.
[That's why I am reaching out to you now with an urgent plea: Can you chip in $25 or more to our grassroots campaign to unseat Troy Balderson, a key Trump ally?](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0017KK1yeYsy40mUOZnb9u-kcYPqXQ1pfj2B6QazT-Jszbqpb8qoZgmTVmcSR5wJnsPkCSlzBUL3phcEDHZ8c6cXGiMdGzLjJTk5YXCKjquWF0KaUDn5MKbBVCF58wyXrjnMY88SeO0S7DaMAzVIWSFO94E_eDMQjOfPxW1PbZiAWvUutW35Tfd2fo3NBOghzK9TstrGACDc3iVOaVHRWsHSrKC4naz0_mZ&c=n7t9SXv7LK9j59mmvRO7CC7_xgmMNpb1aP0a5vUiPI5CHGECnyT_jQ==&ch=NK8DUGClB1ORtkNJsYh-s6C651Jp3mfVTO2MN6KQB8LVWzYTgfdTlg==)

I mean, take a look for yourself, Derek. = The thing about this reunion is that if we make it happen, it could change the trajectory of our country... no offense to Creed. My friend Tim’s seat could very well decide Senate control next year. = To be completely honest with you, Tim is almost a better Senator than he is a musician. Sure he can play the guitar (and the harmonica – he wanted to make sure I told you that, too) but his heart lies within public service. What he’d rather do is work together to build a better Virginia and a better country. We’ve been doing exactly that together for almost 15 years. In a Congress plagued by incessant partisan division, Tim has fought to push through the chaos and represent all Virginians. He’s never faltered in his fight to protect a woman’s right to choose, safeguard voting rights, support military families, tackle gun violence, and protect our environment from the catastrophic events of climate change. If you want to see the Senate under Democratic control again in 2024, we need to support Tim Kaine’s re-election campaign. = Thank you, Virginia Virtuoso’s lead banjo player ******=**** | | Friends of Mark Warner 1490-5A Quarterpath Road #213 Williamsburg, VA 23185 United States | Click here to . | Paid for by Friends of Mark Warner

body:
We’re going to take back power from corrupt politicians like Josh Hawley and put everyday people in charge of our country. Please let me explain.
#
We’ve accomplished so much together this year, Peter.
From launching this campaign on January 6th to calling out Josh Hawley on cable news to breaking Missouri fundraising records, your support has helped us put a national spotlight on this U.S. Senate race.
**And now, multiple polls are showing that we’re in a neck-and-neck race with Josh Hawley — the GOP’s most unpopular U.S. Senator running in 2024.**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40447?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B)
In a moment, I’m going to ask you to add your first donation of any amount toward my campaign to defeat Hawley and flip Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat. **But first, please let me share a little more about how we got here.**
**[ADD A DONATION NOW →](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40447?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B)**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40447?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B)
I grew up in mid-Missouri. And like so many other Americans, my family lived paycheck-to-paycheck. So when my little sister was born with a heart condition, the medical bills bankrupted us. Maxed-out credit cards and no money left, times had never been tougher.
But we weren’t alone — our community took care of us. When my parents had to take my sister to the hospital in St. Louis, our neighbors and friends took my siblings and me into their homes and brought more meals by the house than we could ever hope to eat. **That’s the Missouri I grew up in.**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40447?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B)
Their support helped send me to college, and after that I joined the Marines to honor everything they had done for me and my family growing up. Got deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan. Later the Pentagon. I was on the Joint Staff negotiating arms control agreements with NATO and Russia.
When I came home between tours in Iraq and Afghanistan, one of the hardest things was seeing what was happening back in my old neighborhood. It was a community picked for parts — the local corner store boarded up, my first family house bulldozed to the ground. **Here’s all that’s left of it:**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40447?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B)
While all of us were risking our lives building up towns like Habbaniyah, Fallujah, and Herat, career politicians like Josh Hawley let our country waste away. They spent trillions on bailouts, tax breaks, and subsidies for the industries that stripped our communities for parts — like Wall Street, Big Pharma, and Big Oil — and then told us they can’t figure out how to invest even a fraction of that into building up our own country and investing in our own people.
**I saw what was happening — and I was ready to fight back.**
So in my final year of active duty, I worked to upend the corporate defense monopolies that leave our country less safe. I also joined an organization that fights corporate monopolies — we took on defense contractors, Big Pharma, Big Tech, Big Ag, Wall Street. The people buying off our politicians and leaving the rest of us behind.
**And now, I’m running for U.S. Senate to replace Josh Hawley and fundamentally change who has power in our country** — so everyday people call the shots, not massive corporations or corrupt politicians. I want to abolish corporate PACs, expose lobbyists writing our laws, criminalize war profiteering, ban insider trading among members of Congress, and enact a Marshall Plan for the Midwest — a massive investment and job creation program that will rebuild our forgotten communities and get us off fossil fuels once and for all.
I want to codify Roe v. Wade, secure voting rights, and ban anti-union “Right-to-Work” scams forever. I want to put working people in charge of our country. But I need your help to get it done.
**Without a single cent of corporate PAC money, we’re building the people-powered movement that's going to defeat Josh Hawley and flip this Senate seat — and I need you on our team.[Please add a donation of any amount right now so we can continue building this movement and finally give power back to everyday, working people.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40447?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=6&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B)**
If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution instantly:
[Contribute $10](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40448?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=10&t=7&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B) [Contribute $25](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40448?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=8&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B) [Give another amount](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40447?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=9&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B)
---
I’m not just running to make a point — **this is a race we can win.**
**Josh Hawley is vulnerable.** In 2018, he won his seat with only 51% of the vote — and after he exposed himself to be a fraud and a coward on January 6th, he became the least popular Republican Senator up for re-election in 2024. In Missouri’s last Senate race during a presidential election, the margin was only 2.7%.
Since Hawley was elected, Missourians have broken with him and taken back their power at the ballot box by voting to raise the minimum wage, expand Medicaid through the Affordable Care Act, and legalize cannabis.
TIME Magazine called me the “clean-cut, populist Marine veteran who could give Democrats a fighting chance." And if we’re able to get this message in front of voters early in this race, we have a real shot at defeating Josh Hawley in 2024 and flipping Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat.
**But I need you on this team to get it done, Peter.** GOP insiders and even Hawley’s own campaign have already started attacking me — and over the coming months, they’re bound to get even more vicious. That’s why we need to start preparing right now to fight back and deliver our positive message to voters.
**[Will you chip in anything you can right now so we can keep building this record-breaking grassroots movement and stay prepared for the fight ahead? I don’t take a cent from corporate PACs, so I mean it when I say anything makes a big difference to our campaign.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/40447?refcode=em20231222-4439&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=10&akid=4439%2E614464%2Ex_8t6B)**

Thanks for helping us get it done,
Lucas Kunce

**GET TO KNOW VIVEK:** Vivek is an American entrepreneur, political and cultural thought leader, and New York Times bestselling author of **_Woke, Inc.: Inside Corporate America's Social Justice Scam_** , along with his second book, **_Nation of Victims: Identity Politics, the Death of Merit, and the Path Back to Excellence_**.

He has been a prominent and outspoken critic against ESG, discriminatory practices under the guise of critical race theory, and of what he calls "government-tech censorship," where the government colludes with big tech to do through the backdoor what it couldn't do through the front door under the Constitution.

Vivek is a first-generation American. Growing up in the Cincinnati area, he often recounts the sage advice he received from his father that "If you're going to stand out, then you might as well be outstanding." This advice set the course for his life: an accomplished pianist, a nationally ranked tennis player, and the valedictorian of his Jesuit high school. He went on to graduate summa cum laude in Biology from Harvard in 2007 and received his J.D. degree from Yale Law School in 2013, worked at a hedge fund, then started a pharmaceutical company, Roivant Sciences, where his team developed five drugs that went on to become FDA-approved.

In 2022, he founded Strive Asset Management, an Ohio-based firm, that takes direct aim at asset managers like BlackRock, State Street, Vanguard and others for their fiduciary breach of duty to maximize the wealth of their clients for Wokeism. Strive's mission is to restore the voices of everyday citizens in the American economy by leading companies to focus on excellence over politics.

Friend, You have an opportunity to help correct one of the worst injustices of the Covid era. **Thou****sands of hardworking, competent people were fired -- all because they refused to get the Covid shot.** Doctors, nurses, teachers, members of the military, and many more. But the Symphony rejected ALL of them and put them on a year of UNPAID LEAVE. These three musicians were Buddhist, Christian and Jewish. **To you and me, the freedom to practice your religion is a sacred right.** **So is your right to bodily autonomy.** But in the eyes of the cultural Marxists who control so many institutions in America today, your body doesn't belong to you - it belongs to them. They'll decide where you go... They'll decide what you need... They'll decide what you can have... They'll decide what vaccines you must take... In other words: _Your individual liberties_ will cease to exist. The good news is that while cultural Marxism is popular on college campuses, legacy media press rooms, the boardrooms of woke companies and inside government bureaucracies... ...the vast majority of Americans are against it. Because it was never about "science" or "health" - it was always about control. And it's time to tell the cultural Marxists who want to control every aspect of your life that we aren't backing down. Peter, from the moment the USPS Board of Governors selected GOP megadonor and Trump supporter Louis DeJoy as postmaster general, our nation’s postal service has suffered.

In fall 2020 – a moment when, in a swell of true democracy, there was a record number of mail-in ballots – mail delivery slowed _drastically_ under DeJoy's control. In some areas, on-time mail delivery fell to 60% during the election months.

This wasn’t DeJoy’s only alarming move. He also stood in stark opposition to President Biden’s plan to help the USPS transition to all-electric vehicles in an effort to fight climate change. In fact, DeJoy went as far as launching his own plan to replace the majority of the USPS fleet with gas-powered trucks.
**But Louis DeJoy’s worst offense by _far_ ****is his treatment of USPS mail carriers.**

DeJoy is overworking mail carriers, cutting their pay, and _refusing_ to staff up after many employees have quit due to deteriorating working conditions. This has, in turn, led to the remaining workers being overworked to a dangerous and sometimes _deadly_ degree.

Polling shows that this race is anyone's to win. (A large number of voters are undecided!) But experts have said that I'm at a serious fundraising deficit compared to my opponents, and I need every dollar I can get to close this gap. So I need to pick up steam and build up resources quickly – and the only way to do it is to hit my mid-month fundraising goal.

Running a campaign in California is expensive – and political experts are saying this could be the most competitive Senate primary in U.S. history. **With two other candidates in this race sitting on millions, missing my goal could spell disaster for this campaign.**

Grassroots supporters like you are propelling this campaign to monumental heights. And this grassroots team is the reason political pundits across the board are saying this race is wide open.

So here I am, writing to you again, Peter. I know you hear a lot from me, but it's only because I trust you and believe that I can't do this without you. **[Please, if you can split a donation between myself and The Collective PAC before our end-of-year deadline to help close our fundraising gap, it would mean the world to me.](https://an.collectivepac.org/ss/c/wehEm_vu1NBVXOKYSqOxTOi34aJoCJC1EivM7Ih953z13Gsiw4jYjb8npbjGXirZLt3B3YmMzfTeaUv6D3l9TDms7SZmz4-Gf7x7MJr2Ctk3s3g6PmmKV6Blt5TiZM6TtC9LWlxic176-2GZUKtcBGFlmOA85TCV16-juPZXanvbUvkNx4KcvTpxsf_mkLkHWbJIVn4WrqO9IuP3X3u5Yhua0SsatsNPfK2eKpefsPpSDxH4RefbfVr0FM1yoz1wd1Wn22MnRRUGkbR6ra44Xm0QRJJ_ywykZliqv9N-DF8vFyXBJSoGtAg-MC3L5f3GWaOTS32Ee_TYvh8czpMP2ohiMYSRU3twCI29r1nO99JpvDDAhPBJKHFeO2puR0iX8-NGUccxHINeirytyIM_F3O4KnyjrO1Q8YfHJQOl4S_rxwNdUmA3L3iYAh8eEGvw/42c/rlSEiqtOSLW4sJSvS4yOLQ/h2/HT2qE52C76WNYifxmUqVS_-WrKVT7Xgr7FAKq9bvHuc)** | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will be processed immediately and split between Barbara Lee and The Collective PAC.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Before Donald Trump rode down that elevator in 2015
disclaimer_text: Paid for by The Long Run PAC, P
body:
#
No matter who the GOP nominates for President — twice-impeached, can-barely-even-count-how-many-times-indicted Donald Trump, or one of his enablers — it’s clear that the Republican party has chosen a path of dangerous extremism and is spreading it up and down the ballot and across the country.
We cannot go down that path with them.
If MAGA Republicans take back more power, they’ll further restrict the right to an abortion nationwide, the freedom to vote, and protections for trans people. They’ll threaten Social Security and Medicare, reward the rich and powerful, and embolden an extremist base across the country.
So I’m fighting to stop the GOP’s dangerous agenda, protect our freedoms, and pass policies that put our government on the side of working families. That means passing national abortion protections. That means strengthening our democracy and protecting voting rights. That means defending LGBTQ+ rights.
But here’s the way I see it: This critical election is not only about fighting back against MAGA extremism. We must also rip out the root causes of the deep problems in our economy, our government, and our democracy. The problems that existed way before Donald Trump rode down that elevator in 2015.
So I'll be direct: We’re up against a lot of problems right now. We not only have to fight back against MAGA extremism — but also against a system that benefits from the status quo and says that big change is “impossible.”
That’s what some told me about my idea of a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — an agency that has returned more than $16 billion to American consumers who’ve been cheated. I was also told that my plan for student debt cancelation wouldn’t be possible either — but President Biden has still been able to cancel around $127 billion in student debt so far for nearly 3.6 million borrowers.
[**I’ve got a whole bunch more plans for what we can accomplish with a Democratic House, a Democratic Senate, and a Democratic White House in 2025. If you’re able to donate today, you’ll help ensure that I can keep fighting in the Senate and we can make these plans a reality. Can you please split $5 between The Long Run and my campaign as we work to start 2024 with the strongest momentum possible?**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=longrunpac-em-warren-split.-45zWj&refcode=em231222-1-t2&t=1&akid=5093%2E196590%2EL6YXYR)
We can do this. We can beat the extreme MAGA vision of a country that has fewer freedoms, fewer working people able to make ends meet, and fewer voices in our democracy. A movement that wants our country to have more corruption, more extremist laws, and more struggle for working families.
And we can also make sure that our country isn’t only working for people at the top, but for everyone. We can reimagine our tax code, with billionaires and giant corporations paying a fair share. We can pass universal child care. We can reform the Supreme Court. We can end the filibuster.
This remarkable moment in our history is an opportunity for our country to shake off who we were and build something new, but not a guarantee that it will happen. Because you don’t get what you don’t fight for.
I’m in this fight all the way — are you with me?
[**A contribution today will help fend off any potential challengers and make sure we start 2024 with strong momentum for our campaign. So can you please split $5 or anything you can between my campaign and The Long Run?**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=longrunpac-em-warren-split.-45zWj&refcode=em231222-1-t2&t=2&akid=5093%2E196590%2EL6YXYR)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

clean_body: 2024 could be another "Year of the Woman" | = Peter, it's Ellen. To me, it's clear as day that Democrats are more fired up than ever to elect pro-choice women. This year, Democratic pro-choice women defeated Republicans at the ballot box, cementing control of both chambers of the Virginia General Assembly. A pro-choice governor was reelected in deep-red Kentucky. Ohio voters successfully enshrined abortion access in their state's constitution. Choice was on the ballot, and choice won. I've seen this kind of grassroots energy before. In 1992, EMILYs List grew our membership by 600% and elected four new women to the Senate and 20 to the House. It quickly became known as the "Year of the Woman," but none of this work was accomplished overnight. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = I've seen a lot as the founder of EMILYs List. We were a much smaller organization in 1991, when women across the country were fed up with anti-choice extremists making decisions about our fundamental rights. (Sound familiar?!) That anger inspired a nationwide demand for better representation, and the growing EMILYs List community laid the groundwork for a sea change in American politics. We started early, and our efforts were born out on Election Day 1992. Now, 2024 is quickly approaching. The ultraconservative Supreme Court has overturned Roe v. Wade , and 21 states have banned or severely restricted abortion access. And just like in 1992,we are fighting back . After this year's victories, the groundwork is clearly set to make 2024 another "Year of the Woman," but we can't let up on our work for even a second. Senate candidates like Angela Alsobrooks and Elissa Slotkin , and House candidates like Allyson Muñiz Damikolas and Michelle Vallejo can make all of the difference for abortion rights next November — but only with your support. It's all hands on deck. **So that's why I'm asking, Peter: as 2023 comes to a close, will you help Democratic pro-choice women make 2024 another "Year of the Woman?" Donate now to support candidates who can restore abortion access across the country: =** Thank you for being with EMILYs List in this fight, Ellen R. Fellow American,

The Washington Legislature will convene for regular session in early January, which makes for an interesting twist in my campaign for Governor.

In Washington, statewide elected officials are **prohibited from fundraising beginning one month before legislative session (December 8, 2023) until session concludes (March 7, 2024).** So, from December 8, 2023, to March 7, 2024, my opponent Bob Ferguson cannot raise ANY campaign dollars. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: I’m running for re-election to hold the line against MAGA Republican extremists and make our country work for everyone, not just the rich and powerful. And I’m asking you to stay in the fight by my side.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Republican operatives, special interests, Big Tech moguls, Wall Street executives, and far-right ideologues are looking for signs of weakness.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=1869%2E4032634%2EK_Xu6G)
---
Campaigns are chock-full of surprises, but you can count on some events like clockwork. And one of them’s coming up fast. In just a few weeks, we’ll file an official report with the FEC on our fundraising for October, November, and December. The numbers will be public. Then Republican operatives, special interests, Big Tech moguls, Wall Street executives, and far-right ideologues will scour them for any signs of weakness. Not just because they want to defeat me for re-election — but also because they want to prove that there isn’t enough momentum for our progressive agenda. But a whole bunch of $3 donations add up fast to demonstrate widespread support for ending Washington corruption, ensuring the right to an abortion, guaranteeing universal child care, getting the wealthy to pay their fair share, tackling corporate price gouging, and putting power in the hands of working people. [**So, we've got to show the far right that there’s a big, tough team fighting for this campaign and this mission. And one of the best ways to do that is by making a donation before the end of the year. Can you make a donation of $28 or any amount by December 31 to help make our next FEC fundraising report — the last before our election year — as strong as possible?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1052?amount=28&t=8&akid=1869%2E4032634%2EK_Xu6G)

---
_If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically:_ |
---

---
| [DONATE NOW: $28](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1052?t=26&express_lane=true&amount=28&akid=1869%2E4032634%2EK_Xu6G)
---
| [DONATE NOW: $50](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1052?t=28&express_lane=true&amount=50&akid=1869%2E4032634%2EK_Xu6G)
---
| [DONATE NOW: $100](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1052?t=18&express_lane=true&amount=100&akid=1869%2E4032634%2EK_Xu6G)
---
| [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1052?t=20&express_lane=true&akid=1869%2E4032634%2EK_Xu6G)
---

---
The total amount we raise is an important stat, to be sure, but I’ll really have my eye on something else: The number of people who make a contribution. Because the number of people who contribute — no matter the amount — demonstrates just how many people are still in this fight. That number demonstrates the amount of people who are linking arms and fighting for the bold reforms our country needs — from taxing the rich so we can fund opportunity for all of our kids, to rooting corruption out of Washington so we can put our government on the side of working families. With this final fundraising report of 2023, we’ve got one last chance to demonstrate the strength of our campaign as we head into 2024. And you don’t need me to tell you everything that’s on the line next year. The right to an abortion. The future of bedrock policies like Social Security and Medicare. Our democracy itself. In the face of big threats, we can whimper. We can whine. Or we can fight back. Me? I’m fighting back. I’m running for re-election to hold the line against MAGA Republican extremists and make our country work for everyone, not just the rich and powerful. And I’m asking you to stay in the fight by my side. **[If it makes sense for you right now, please chip in $28 or any amount to help win this re-election campaign and help put power in the hands of working people.](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1052?amount=28&t=14&akid=1869%2E4032634%2EK_Xu6G)** Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

body:
Marginalized communities are feeling unheard and betrayed. | | |
---
Friend, Our government continues to find billions of U.S. taxpayer dollars to fund war, while claiming there's not enough to meet Americans’ basic needs, including clean drinking water. Amidst a rise in antisemitic, Islamophobic, and anti-Arab hate crimes, we also continue to see violence against Black people, Indigenous people, other people of color, and LGBTQ+ people. **Marginalized communities are feeling unheard and betrayed by their political representatives. There's still so much to do to build the true multiracial democracy we need, and to ensure our communities’ safety and well-being.** So many local and state elected officials have supported our work on securing human rights such as access to clean water, pushed back on “development” projects that push out our residents, taken on corporate polluters, and now back our demand for a permanent ceasefire. As we head into a critical election year, **we’ve got to raise money to support progressives in our movement, who are facing millions of dollars in attacks from far-right groups.** [**To help build a Last year in Michigan, my Rooted in Community Leadership PAC supported dozens of candidates and grassroots organizations at the state and local level―donating more than $128,000 to build progressive political power and invest directly in our communities.
The Rooted in Community Leadership PAC helps us support causes throughout the district. It's also how we support progressive candidates who are rooted in and truly represent their communities.
**We’re making investments in community-based groups that are lifting up those most in need, and supporting progressive candidates who are under relentless attack for pushing for the bold changes we deserve.**
Even though 80% of Democrats support a ceasefire, their representatives are not listening. Recently, we learned that the anti-Palestinian group AIPAC is planning to spend at least $100 million in an attempt to defeat me and other progressive candidates who have had the courage to speak out and demand a ceasefire.
**We need more elected leaders from the local, state, and federal level who truly represent the people and who are advocating for the changes our communities desperately need.** We can’t let far-right mega-donors**** undermine our democracy **or** intimidate our movement for change.

Amidst a rise in antisemitic, Islamophobic, and anti-Arab hate crimes, we also continue to see violence against Black people, Indigenous people, other people of color, and LGBTQ+ people. Marginalized communities are feeling unheard and betrayed by their political representatives. There's still so much to do to build the true multiracial democracy we need, and to ensure our communities’ safety and well-being. So many local and state elected officials have supported our work on securing human rights such as access to clean water, pushed back on “development” projects that push out our residents, taken on corporate polluters, and now back our demand for a permanent ceasefire. As we head into a critical election year, we’ve got to raise money to support progressives in our movement, who are facing millions of dollars in attacks from far-right groups. | Last year in Michigan, my Rooted in Community Leadership PAC supported dozens of candidates and grassroots organizations at the state and local level―donating more than $128,000 to build progressive political power and invest directly in our communities. The Rooted in Community Leadership PAC helps us support causes throughout the district. It's also how we support progressive candidates who are rooted in and truly represent their communities. We’re making investments in community-based groups that are lifting up those most in need, and supporting progressive candidates who are under relentless attack for pushing for the bold changes we deserve. Words and actions have consequences. **Back in 2022,** Kari called for board supervisors to ignore the law and their duty to Arizonans and delay the election certification in Arizona. | | **_The Texas Tribune:_
"Gov. Greg Abbott signs bill making illegal immigration a state crime"******

Greg Abbott is attempting to scare Hispanic people in Texas to score political points with MAGA Republicans. **[Brian is ready to go to Washington to fight for a border that is humanely and effectively secured and comprehensive immigration reform>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/75647091/445318244/1416552317?refcode=em23_231222_ImmFR_fnd_gq_act___TW_ettx&utm_campaign=em23_231222_ImmFR_fnd_gq_act___TW_ettx&utm_medium=email&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&firstname=Peter&lastname=&zip=&refcode2=39c50228-e9a0-ee11-bea1-002248223f36&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU5MjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzljNTAyMjgtZTlhMC1lZTExLWJlYTEtMDAyMjQ4MjIzZjM2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NJNgkO6TEpcUuzoNbabJJLaZVcgtt0hPkOfKKAA3oc4=)** Peter —

As an Air Force Veteran and a Texan, Brian recognizes it’s critical our borders are secure. He knows keeping our communities safe AND providing opportunities for hardworking people to come here legally and strengthen our communities are not mutually exclusive.

The bill signed on Monday by Governor Abbott is one of the most extreme in the country and will likely result in racial profiling, violations of due process, and the targeting of US citizens and permanent residents. This bill is another in a long line of attacks by Governor Abbott and Texas Republicans on marginalized communities.

That's why in Congress Brian will:
* Pass comprehensive immigration reform that **includes an earned pathway to citizenship for current immigrants** so those who have followed the rules can come out of the shadows and continue to build their lives and strengthen our communities.
* Support investments in **effective border security technology** and appropriate staffing of ports of entry.
* Ensure border enforcement is done **humanely and in accordance with our values as a country** , and that we’ll never lock up and separate kids from their families again.
* Pass legislation **permanently protecting DREAMERs.**
* Ensure that **actions taken to secure Texas’ border do not displace or hurt the health of historically marginalized communities,** while also protecting our natural resources and beautiful landscapes in South Texas.

# 2023 December e-newsletter
News and information for District 5 in San Mateo County.
---
|
---
|
---
| **Happy holidays to you and yours**
---
| Dear friends,

As the holidays draw closer and we approach 2024, I am so thankful to serve as your San Mateo County Supervisor. I am also thankful for my wife Ana and son Piero, who both remind me every day how fortunate I am to have family by my side.

Piero was born during my first year in office and watching him grow up is the joy of our lives. He loves to read, play sports and has a love for life that is truly inspiring. I am also grateful to my staff for helping me to address the needs of my constituents in San Mateo County and for creating policy that will improve the lives of all county residents.

Some policies I sponsored this year and are now county law include one of the strictest anti-tobacco ordinances in the state that severely fines retailers for selling prohibited nicotine products and selling any tobacco products to minors; a guaranteed income pilot program for non-minor dependents transitioning out of foster care; and the Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operations ordinance which allows home cooks to start their own businesses and legally sell hot food dishes out of their homes with the potential to earn up to $100,000 a year.
---
I’m proud to say MEHKO has created 32 new businesses in the county including the Pearl Kitchen and the Baking Endeavor in Daly City.

I am also honored to announce a significant one-time grant of district-discretionary Measure K funds of $75,000 I granted to the Daly City/Colma Chamber of Commerce. This strategic investment will not only sustain its crucial operations but also establish a pivotal business resource center.

I also awarded the city of Brisbane a $200,000 grant in Measure K district-discretionary funds to replace the aging boiler at the community pool — a significant consumer of fossil fuels — with cutting-edge electric heat pump water heaters.

As I finish my seventh year in office, I am honored to be a member of a Board of Supervisors that has made historic investments in reducing homelessness, creating affordable housing, removing guns from our streets, making historical investments in mental health services, and protecting our environment.

As the year comes to an end, I’d like to thank you all for taking the time to read my monthly newsletters and for your support.

Happy holidays and happy new year from my family to yours!
---
| **I’m proud to be honored by the California Alliance for Jobs** I was so honored to be proclaimed the Regional Leadership Champion by the California Alliance for Jobs at a special reception at Westlake Joes’s in Daly City Monday, December 4. When government works with our business community and unions, we have the power to train the next generation of residents seeking construction careers. Investing in job-creating infrastructure is a proven strategy to change lives in our communities.

Special thanks to California Lt. Gov. Eleni Kounalakis, state Sen. Scott Wiener, Assemblymember Diane Papan and San Francisco Assessor Joaquin Torres for speaking on the value of working together to promote job creation and training in the state of California.

Thanks also to Metropolitan Transportation Commission Executive Director Andrew Fremier, SFO General Manager Ivar Satero and other transportation leaders for advancing a 21st Century vision for the Bay Area and beyond and the investments in infrastructure that will make it happen.

Special shout out to John Duggan of Joe’s of Westlake, Chris Gruwell and Joshua Arce for making it happen.

Representing over 2,000 heavy construction companies and 80,000 union construction workers from Bakersfield to the Oregon border, the California Alliance for Jobs (CAJ) is a unique labor-management partnership that advocates for responsible investments in public infrastructure projects.

CAJ keeps California’s people and economy moving as the state’s population grows by focusing on improving water systems, expanding transportation networks and increasing the access and quality of our public infrastructure.

To learn more go to: [https://www.rebuildca.org/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=14e91b3735&e=c0babbc643)
---
---
| **
County funds major flood and climate adaptation project with $15 million** When Lake Merced overflows, it floods 5 hours later in unincorporated Broadmoor Village and Daly City, with the damage sometimes being extensive to properties and vehicles.

This is a problem I have been advocating to fix since my time serving on the Daly City Council starting back in 2009 and I’m proud to announce San Mateo County has invested $15 million in this very important climate mitigation infrastructure project.

As part of the Vista Grande Project, Daly City, the lead agency on the project, will expand the capacity of the Vista Grande tunnel in order to better manage conveyance of stormwater to the Pacific Ocean. These efforts would reduce uncontrolled overflows from the Vista Grande Canal into Lake Merced, while achieving a sustained increase in Lake Merced water levels, improving storm water quality, and providing further restoration of the drainage basin's natural hydrology.

It's a partnership between the North San Mateo County Sanitation District, the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission, which is pitching in $35 million for the project, and Caltrans, which has committed another $3.6 million to the project. The National Parks Service and other regulatory agencies have been involved with the approvals since it involves Fort Funston and the project should get started in 2025.
---
| **
$147 million Wellness Center to address health care needs of underserved north county residents**

The Board of Supervisors just committed $145 million toward the construction of a new health campus to deliver primary patient care for residents in north San Mateo County, a traditionally underserved population.

The 77,000 square-foot South San Francisco Wellness Center will be a new health center and office building which will expand the San Mateo County Health System’s ability to deliver health care services beyond its main campus in the city of San Mateo.

The Wellness Center will house a medical clinic, other county departments and Aging and Adult Services, which care for older and dependent adults, including abuse prevention, public guardian and authority, in-home care, nutritious meals and more.

The three-story clinic will provide primary and pediatric care, express care, dental and optometry services under federal guidelines; women, infants and children health care services; a multi-purpose conference area that can also operate as an Emergency Response Center; and two floors of office space.

This wellness center will serve the health care needs of north county residents for generations to come and I can’t wait to cut the ribbon on it when it opens to the public.
---
| **
County grant supports domestic violence awareness**

A new documentary I funded with a $75,000 district-discretionary Measure K grant has just been released by the Ariana Mae Hatami Foundation called the “Spirit of Ariana” that you can watch here: www.spiritofariana.com.

It’s a sequel to a 2020 documentary I funded called “Message from Ariana,” a film to inform our community how to recognize the signs and dangers of domestic violence.

“Message from Ariana” was created in collaboration with the San Mateo County Board of Education, the San Mateo Department of Justice, and others; it is currently being utilized throughout the county in high schools, community colleges, CORA, as well as the County of San Mateo District Attorney’s Office, Victim Services Division.

The sequel, which also covers the reality of human trafficking, will be used to reinforce insight to prevention of violence while at the same time will provide hope and healing for the survivors and hopefully save lives.

Intimate partner violence impacts 1 out of 3 women in the world. This devastating loss reminds us that we must continue efforts to create more tools and resources for the survivors of domestic abuse and allies to recognize the signs of domestic abuse.

Ariana Mae Hatami was killed on December 17, 2016 by a man she was living in who was also her coworker. In August of that same year, Ariana was struck twice in the face by the man who was later convicted of misdemeanor domestic violence.

Ariana’s parents formed the foundation in her honor with a mission statement that reads: Transforming a heart-shattering tragedy into hope for victims of violence. To learn more about San Mateo County’s domestic violence response go here: https://www.smcgov.org/hsa/domestic-violence.

**Measure K Oversight Committee seeking member from District 5**

The Measure K Oversight Committee has a vacant seat to fill for residents in my supervisorial District 5.

The Measure K Oversight Committee ensures the completion of, and reviews the results of, an annual audit of the Measure K sales and use tax revenues received by the County, reviews and recommends appropriate metrics to assess the impact of Measure K funds and prepares an annual report. The Committee does not make funding recommendations. Members meet at least twice a year and is not compensated.

The direct link to the online application is here: [https://www.smcgov.org/bnc/application-boards-commissions-and-committees](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=14230530e8&e=c0babbc643)

Go here for a link to all county commission vacancies and to apply: [https://www.smcgov.org/bnc/vacancies](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=43dd0ba689&e=c0babbc643)
---
| **Interns wanted to join our team ** We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: [https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=e4baadcd74&e=c0babbc643). You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at [mrichardson@smcgov.org](mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org). ** **
---
| **Battling food insecurity **
Food insecurity is a problem some residents may still face as we continue to emerge from the pandemic. Here are some resources residents can access: **CalFresh:**
Is a program for people with low-income who meet federal income eligibility rules and want to add to their budget to put healthy and nutritious food on the table. Website: [https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-nutrition/calfresh](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=f1a56318f1&e=c0babbc643) Contact: (650) 802-6576, [antorres@smcgov.org](mailto:antorres@smcgov.org) **Daly City Partnership:**
DC Partnership is a local partnership that was formed to guide collaborative efforts and connect our community to services that promote well-being. Check out their website for times and locations. Website: [https://www.dcpartnership.org/covid19/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=2607ef03dc&e=c0babbc643) **Second Harvest Food Bank:**
Second Harvest offers food at various locations throughout San Mateo County listed on its webpage. Website: [https://www.shfb.org/get-food/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=de9f5a01e8&e=c0babbc643) Contacts: Call (800) 984-3663 or text GETFOOD to (408) 455-5181 **Interns wanted to join our team **

We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: [https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=b944706ed5&e=c0babbc643). You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at [mrichardson@smcgov.org](mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org) In friendship,
David J. Canepa

# **A Message from the Chairwoman**
---
| | ** _Merry Christmas!_**
---
Friends, From all of us at Indiana GOP HQ, we want to wish you a very Merry Christmas!!! This is a time for each of us to step away from the hustle and bustle, and spend quality time with friends and family recharging for the year ahead! 2023 has been an amazing year and it's all because of the hard work, dedication, and sacrifice from each of you. We have a built a GREAT Republican team and we are looking forward to 2024!!! 2024 is going to be a HUGE Election year for our state and our country -- together we will make sure we put America on the right track and that Indiana continues to be a state that others admire and envy. Thank you for all that you do.
---
---
Chairwoman Anne F. Hathaway
---
| |
# **Governor Eric Holcomb's Week in Review**
---
| |
# _Gov. Holcomb Sat Down for Multiple End of Year Interviews_
---
---
| | [](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/eb17e182de6198f03947229f28c3afba/7cf296c7c1c6e754c3d6b838967d376c/40313)**Governor Eric Holcomb **[sat down](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/eb17e182de6198f03947229f28c3afba/29ad394e775036f6c3d6b838967d376c/40313) for multiple end of year interviews this week, in which he reflected on his 7 years in office and what is coming in 2024. **What he’s saying** : "Next year will be about landing and launching, meaning landing certain projects or deals and finishing what we started and then launching new. I don’t want there to be a sense in this administration that we’re just landing planes safely. We have to be launching”, **[**Gov. Holcomb**](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/eb17e182de6198f03947229f28c3afba/acb4166e87b9cb3dc3d6b838967d376c/40313)** said in an interview with the Indiana Capital Chronicle. **What else happened this week?[Gov. Holcomb](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/eb17e182de6198f03947229f28c3afba/3a0ab85e0631afb8c3d6b838967d376c/40313) **sent out a reminder that this tax season, Indiana National Guardsmen will no longer have to pay state income tax. This is thanks to House Bill 1034 that the General Assembly passed and Gov. Holcomb signed into law in 2023. [**Gov. Holcomb**](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/eb17e182de6198f03947229f28c3afba/100ed3bd0d70d2b7c3d6b838967d376c/40313) also announced a $127 million MEGA Grant to INDOT for the FlexRoad project in Northwest Indiana.
* To stay up-to-date, follow **Gov. Holcomb** on [Facebook](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/eb17e182de6198f03947229f28c3afba/1066ce6c5376898fc3d6b838967d376c/40313) or [Twitter](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/eb17e182de6198f03947229f28c3afba/cda08c5bbfa55f1cc3d6b838967d376c/40313).

# ✅ _2023 End of Year Recap_

---
| | 2023 has been an extremely successful year for Hoosiers. Republican leadership continues to make Indiana one of the best places to live. At the local level, we secured a record 76 mayors statewide. This includes flipping 14 mayors’ offices across the state. Our Republican Diversity Leadership Series continues to grow the party and reach new members, including two alumni being elected to local offices. And Republican led cities in Indiana continue to rank nationally among the best places to live! In the State Legislature this year, Republicans really focused on making sure your state government is working for you. Here are just a few things Republicans were able to accomplish: \- Increased pay for state police, state conservation officers, and state excise police \- Approved a $7 million investment into regional firefighting training infrastructure and an additional $10 million to help purchase equipment for volunteer firefighter organizations - Increased K-12 funding with an additional $1.5 BILLION in new money, including teacher pay raises and covering the costs of textbooks for all Hoosier families. Republicans accomplished all this while also lowering taxes and balancing the budget! We’re so thankful for all of these successes this year.

| | Peter, fun fact: you probably know that the Declaration of Independence was signed in Philadelphia in 1776, but did you also know that Philly was the capital of the United States from 1790 to 1800?

I’m one of our Commonwealth’s number one fans, so there’s a lot more where that came from, and our friends down in GA wanted me to share some PA facts with you.

Before I share, my Finance Director, Taylor, said that I can’t use this email to only recite facts about Pennsylvania, no matter how much I might want to. I should also ask folks to chip in to help me continue representing the place I’ve always called home.

[**_Peter, will you split a contribution between my campaign and the GA Dems to help me continue fighting for my fellow Pennsylvanians in the U.S. Senate?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/75653200/445332257/1703534649?refcode=20231221.2_BC_12AF&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3OGU0Zjc2ZC1lZmEwLWVlMTEtYmVhMS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AIQj4qRluKZhshtccMEkzL3tjcuC4AMdMIgmYWTBMY8=)

Now that’s out of the way, are you ready for some more facts?

Did you know that Pennsylvania’s Fayette County is home to Fort Necessity, where George Washington experienced his first military combat in 1754? | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/75653201/445332258/1703534649?refcode=20231221.2_BC_12AF&amount=20&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3OGU0Zjc2ZC1lZmEwLWVlMTEtYmVhMS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AIQj4qRluKZhshtccMEkzL3tjcuC4AMdMIgmYWTBMY8=)
---
Or that William Maclay — a member of Pennsylvania’s first United States Senate delegation — kept a diary during his term, which became one of few historical accounts of the 1st United States Congress?
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/75653202/445332259/1703534649?refcode=20231221.2_BC_12AF&amount=20&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3OGU0Zjc2ZC1lZmEwLWVlMTEtYmVhMS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AIQj4qRluKZhshtccMEkzL3tjcuC4AMdMIgmYWTBMY8=)
---
Or here’s a fun one: the world’s first computer was built in Philadelphia in 1946!
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/75653203/445332260/1703534649?refcode=20231221.2_BC_12AF&amount=20&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3OGU0Zjc2ZC1lZmEwLWVlMTEtYmVhMS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AIQj4qRluKZhshtccMEkzL3tjcuC4AMdMIgmYWTBMY8=)

Friend,
So as not to repeat the mistakes of the past, it's crucial our leaders understand what it takes to defeat terrorism and prevent further humanitarian suffering.
First and foremost, we must recognize Israel's right to self-defense and advocate for the erdication of Hamas as a terrorist organization. We must also draw distinctions between Hamas and innocent Palestinians caught in the crossfire.
The Middle East has been riven with religious and ethnic hatred, colonization, and division by imperial powers for generations. The US played an instrumental role in helping Israel and the Saudi government develop a peace treaty. Hopefully, this was only temporarily stalled by the Hamas attack.
We must learn from historical events, such as Israel's invasion of Southern Lebanon in 1982 in response to a series of terrorist attacks by the Palestinian Liberation Organization, which led to the formation of Hezbollah and, eventually, Hamas.
Back and forth retaliatory attacks — which began just after Israel's founding by the UN in 1948 — have resulted in constant fear and suffering of the Israeli and Palestinian people.
Israel's current approach may not achieve its desired safety, nor may it eliminate terrorist activity.
Instead, it could inadvertently fuel the rise of more terrorist organizations than it destroys and cause future generations to suffer. It has happened before with the Taliban in Afghanistan and the rise of ISIS in Iraq and Syria.
I agree with Sec. of Defense Lloyd Austin when he stated that "the current action can be a tactical win but a strategic loss" for Israel.
I have listed peaceful alternatives here. [https://www.votedrbob.com/post/a-lasting-cure-for-the-people-of-israel-and-palestine-is-needed]
Peace requires more strength than war.
While the work ahead may be challenging, the region can find success. Let us work together to achieve a lasting peace that respects the rights and aspirations of both Palestinians and Israelis.
Regards,
Bob Lorinser

We must also draw distinctions between Hamas and innocent Palestinians caught in the crossfire. The Middle East has been riven with religious and ethnic hatred, colonization, and division by imperial powers for generations. The US played an instrumental role in helping Israel and the Saudi government develop a peace treaty. Hopefully, this was only temporarily stalled by the Hamas attack. We must learn from historical events, such as Israel's invasion of Southern Lebanon in 1982 in response to a series of terrorist attacks by the Palestinian Liberation Organization, which led to the formation of Hezbollah and, eventually, Hamas. Back and forth retaliatory attacks — which began just after Israel's founding by the UN in 1948 — have resulted in constant fear and suffering of the Israeli and Palestinian people. Israel's current approach may not achieve its desired safety, nor may it eliminate terrorist activity. Instead, it could inadvertently fuel the rise of more terrorist organizations than it destroys and cause future generations to suffer. It has happened before with the Taliban in Afghanistan and the rise of ISIS in Iraq and Syria. I agree with Sec. of Defense Lloyd Austin when he stated that "the current action can be a tactical win but a strategic loss" for Israel. I have listed peaceful alternatives here. [] Peace requires more strength than war. While the work ahead may be challenging, the region can find success. Let us work together to achieve a lasting peace that respects the rights and aspirations of both Palestinians and Israelis. Tragically, we are seeing women suffer in states across the country where that right isn’t protected.

EMILY’s List is doing important work to make sure that pro-choice women up and down the ballot are elected throughout the country, and I am excited they are supporting my race here in Virginia — where we’ve never elected a woman as Governor, at least not yet!

My Sisters and Brothers,

Let’s celebrate the season with love and joy! Now is the time to come together as family, friends, and neighbors to create lasting memories filled with warmth and appreciation.

During this special time, let's remember the true meaning of the holidays and the incredible things we can accomplish when we work together. Embrace the magic of the season by sharing hugs, passing down family traditions, playing in the snow, and cozying up for holiday stories with a delicious cup of hot cocoa.

Let's make a difference by giving back - whether it's through volunteering our time or donating to a cause close to our hearts. And don't forget to inspire your loved ones to do the same!

Wishing you peace, love, and abundant happiness. Happy Holidays to all!

Together, #WeRepresent!

Gwen
Proudly representing Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District
Proud Co-Leader of the Violence Against Women Act
100% Pro-Choice
100% Democracy Defender

body:
It’s been an incredible year together

| [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/75655700/445338255/-1341413768?amount=10&refcode=em_fr_2023.12.22_b1_tl_all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NDg5NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MzBmZTViZi1mM2EwLWVlMTEtYmVhMS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iYlfc7iY1VQnVQR8BECRG0Kgber2Z3L0ngh2xAUW40M=)
---
Hi team,

Greg’s top priority in Congress is delivering results for the people of Southwest Ohio. So as 2023 comes to a close, we wanted to highlight just some of what Greg has accomplished during his first year in Congress. | **_DELIVERING FOR SOUTHWEST OHIO’S CHILDREN AND FAMILIES_**
In July, Greg secured **over $14 million in federal funding for local projects.** These projects included:
* Over $900,000 to replace lead water pipes in Southwest Ohio to keep families safe,
* Over $800,000 to renovate the City of Lebanon’s community center for the benefit of the whole community,
* $1,000,000 to improve bus stops and critical transit infrastructure to help people get to work, the grocery store, doctor’s appointments, and more,
* And much more!

**_REACHING ACROSS THE AISLE TO GET RESULTS FOR OH-01_**
Greg was proud to introduce **four bipartisan bills** this year, including the _Child Care Small Business Insight and Improvement Act of 2023_ , which would increase support for small business child care providers.

He also introduced the bipartisan _Medicare PBM Accountability Act_ , which would help lower the cost of prescription drugs for seniors on Medicare.

In September, Greg started the bipartisan What Works Caucus, which aims to bring together Democratic and Republican lawmakers to make data-driven decisions about what federal programs best serve Americans.

_**PUTTING OUR COMMUNITY FIRST**_
Greg’s top priority is always serving people, not playing politics. That’s why, over the past year, Greg and his team hosted **14 town halls** and **resolved over 1,300+ constituent cases**.

By advocating for Southwest Ohio in Congress, Greg has been able to **return over $11 million of federal dollars back to taxpayers and small businesses**.
---
Greg has accomplished so much this year, and we know that none of this would have been possible without your continued support. _Thank you so much for being on our team._ We look forward to all that 2024 will bring!

He also introduced the bipartisan Medicare PBM Accountability Act , which would help lower the cost of prescription drugs for seniors on Medicare. In September, Greg started the bipartisan What Works Caucus, which aims to bring together Democratic and Republican lawmakers to make data-driven decisions about what federal programs best serve Americans. That’s why, over the past year, Greg and his team hosted 14 town halls and resolved over 1,300+ constituent cases. Tester’s open border agenda is **[allowing](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=38654061c62f411fab16b2655f1c3a9c&_e=QqFyk3bcZpEG_SRnillVg5evgxcu-JrYHQOw3rgBUzNQHp-jwhc_rwaMZ2ANuHGZKbCdIENGRyiWWskbKdS8HeMsqE19t_5ts_kSoP0QL6yf66Hpbfv6HoErtZGxX_Enf52FtMFLHAXpovVkyb1ifloWaOCii_zZEw3aUkhkiN6rdpojQZX0-myTWmssr0_shbeuq-Pi-G4AxocmT1JSLdcwWHyvEpWMu1Y7vuBeY6Tx9iNdS6Y30zEe8NjW635HCD42SI-5q2qiZxNcrQv7Sg%3D%3D)** Chinese fentanyl to enter our country, killing over 70,000 Americans a year and becoming the leading cause of death in adults.
